title: Droplet On Tape: Protocol
protocol: Set up the Acoustic Droplet Ejection \(ADE) system using an Olympus V319-SU ultrasonic transducer.
Generate tone-burst signals at the resonance frequency of the transducer (typically 15 MHz).
Amplify the generated tone-burst signals with an Amplifier Research 500A250C RF amplifier to produce a driving voltage around 40 volts.
Route the amplified signal through a bi-directional coupler connected via BNC cable to the ultrasonic transducer.
Eject nano-liter sized droplets by sending the amplified tone-burst to the transducer.
Send a “probe” spike a few milliseconds prior to the ejection tone burst.
Collect the reverse signal from the transducer through the bi-directional coupler.
Monitor the return time and amplitude of the echo signal using an oscilloscope remotely.
Adjust the sample influx rate into the reservoir to maintain the temporal position of the echo.
Maximize the amplitude of the return echo when the transducer is focused on the sample-air interface.
Fix the transducer position once the focus quality is optimized.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl to reconstitute human recombinant leptin.
Sonicate the PI belt in Milli-Q water for 10 minutes.
Sonicate the PI belt in isopropanol for 10 minutes.
Dry the PI belt at 50 °C in a vacuum oven for an hour.
Prepare a 0.25% (w/v) solution of fluoroalkylsilane in n-octane.
Reflux the PI belt in the FAS solution for 2 hours.
Dry the treated PI belt in a vacuum oven at 150 °C for 3 hours.
Mount the system on a Newport UTS-100 motorized stage.
Construct the system using modified Thorlabs aluminum breadboards and mounting brackets.
Drive the conveyor belt with a Lexium M-Drive LMDCE423 micro-stepping stepper motor directly coupled to a 1'' diameter stainless steel shaft.
Operate the drive at an appropriate speed for measurements, typically less than 4 revolutions per second.
Extend the helium environment as far as possible between the sample interaction and the detector.
Use thin inflatable bags to push the extent of the helium environment up to the detector to minimize scatter from heavier atoms in the air.
Run the conveyor belt with no sample being injected onto it while probing the XES signal to detect accumulated sample residue.
Clean the belt by running it over four high pressure (200+ psi) 500 µm I.D. water jets.
Dry the top and bottom of the belt using two compressed Helium blow off nozzles immediately after cleaning.
Draw helium from the Helium chamber and recirculate the gas back into the chamber to power the blow-off nozzles using three gas-tight diaphragm pumps (KNF Neuberger N145.1.2AN.18).
Use a CNC machine to produce a high precision grid of holes.
Position bare ended fibers in the grid of holes.
Align fiber-coupled laser focusing system to the grid of holes by maximizing throughput into the bare ended fibers.
Provide each of three fiber-coupled excitations with 5 degrees of freedom for optimization.
Mount IR emitting fibers in the high precision grid for monitoring droplet arrival time.
Collect excitation light that passes through the belt and sample onto photodiodes during operation.
Monitor signals on remote-accessible oscilloscopes.
Move the laser into the desired position by adjusting a motorized 1 m focal length lens.
Target droplets up to 6 mm in advance of the XFEL interaction region.
Determine the position for specific time delays using a stroboscopic video system.
Observe droplet orthogonal to the beam with a "side-view" camera synchronized to the XFEL.
Adjust the camera delay electronically to match the desired laser delay.
Note the position of the closest droplet to the interaction region when the camera is at zero delay.
Move the laser spot to the noted position for spatial overlap accurate to 100 microns.
Confirm temporal overlap within 200 microseconds using the camera exposure time.
Adjust the deposition delay until a droplet appears in the cross hairs of the XFEL beam as seen on an in-line stroboscopic XFEL synchronized video monitor.
Fine adjust the deposition delay until the droplet is observed to explode while the camera is synchronized with the XFEL arrival.
Change the belt velocity until signal from the two IR gates overlap in time.
Ensure droplets passing over both IR gates are separated by a time equal to the deposition period.
Verify that droplet spacing is an integer multiple of 30 mm and 60 mm.
Adjust belt speed to achieve allowed speeds at a 10 Hz droplet repetition rate.
Dial in fiber excitation delay so it coincides with IR gate signals.
Incrementally adjust deposition delay and belt speed to ensure optical pumps and XFEL hit the droplets.
Pass the conveyor belt through a region of reactive gas.
Create the limits of the reactive gas using differential pumping.
Separate Helium partial pressure from reactive gas partial pressure via small orifices.
Pass the conveyor belt through the series of orifices.
Calculate the exposure time by dividing the extent of the reactive gas L by the tape velocity vtape.
Determine the dead-time by dividing the distance from the end of the reactive gas extent to the XFEL interaction point Lxfel by the tape velocity vtape.
Seal the chamber with vacuum grease, except at the opening and exit holes, to prevent leakage.
